recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what happens to the modulus in the Cosec⁻¹ formula and why.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the Cosec⁻¹ rule and resolve the modulus
steps.margin_note: First mark. The Cosec⁻¹ derivative carries |u| in the denominator. State that e²ˣ⁺¹ is positive for every real x, so |u| = u — do not drop the bars without a reason.
steps.memory_tip: Cosec⁻¹ and Sec⁻¹ are the two inverse derivatives with a modulus. Cosec⁻¹ also carries the minus sign, the same way Cot⁻¹ and Cos⁻¹ do.
lines: An exponential is positive for every real x, so u = e²ˣ⁺¹ > 0 and |u| = e²ˣ⁺¹

recall.must_convey: That d/dx(Cosec⁻¹u) = −1/(|u|√(u² − 1))·du/dx, that du/dx = 2e²ˣ⁺¹, and that |u| = e²ˣ⁺¹ because an exponential is positive.
accept: cosec inverse gives minus one over mod u root u squared minus one
e power two x plus one is always positive so the modulus goes away
the inner derivative is two e power two x plus one
exponential eppudu positive kabatti mod teesesukovacchu
write the modulus and then say it is positive

steps.why: The modulus is part of the formula and is not decoration — it exists because Cosec⁻¹ is defined for u ≤ −1 as well as u ≥ 1. Here u = e²ˣ⁺¹ is positive, so only the branch u ≥ 1 arises, and that branch needs 2x + 1 > 0. Saying why the modulus resolves is what separates a quoted formula from an applied one.
common_mistakes: Dropping the modulus with no reason given.
Writing du/dx = e²ˣ⁺¹ and losing the factor 2 from the exponent.

steps.label: Cancel the exponential and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The e²ˣ⁺¹ on top cancels the one below, and (e²ˣ⁺¹)² = e⁴ˣ⁺² because the powers multiply. Only the 2 remains on top.
steps.memory_tip: Squaring an exponential doubles the whole exponent: (e²ˣ⁺¹)² = e⁴ˣ⁺², not e⁴ˣ⁺¹.
lines: The e²ˣ⁺¹ in the numerator cancels the e²ˣ⁺¹ in the denominator.

recall.must_convey: That the exponentials cancel and (e²ˣ⁺¹)² = e⁴ˣ⁺², giving dy/dx = −2/√(e⁴ˣ⁺² − 1).
accept: the exponential cancels top and bottom leaving minus two
e power two x plus one squared is e power four x plus two
the answer is minus two over root e power four x plus two minus one
exponential cancel ayipothundi, minus two migulutundi
double the exponent when you square it
heard_as: e power four x plus two

steps.why: The cancelling is the reason this answer is short. An examiner reading a long unsimplified fraction cannot tell whether the exponent was squared correctly, so the tidy form also shows the arithmetic.
common_mistakes: Writing (e²ˣ⁺¹)² as e⁴ˣ⁺¹, doubling only part of the exponent.
Cancelling the exponential but keeping the minus sign off the answer.

insider_note: An exponential is always positive, so |u| = u and the modulus in the Cosec⁻¹ rule can be dropped. The e²ˣ⁺¹ then cancels top and bottom.
